solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Feel bias of some sort? It's possible

indicators.note: a feel and bias 'of some sort' are these letters in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A question of whether one might detect prejudice, answered with a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of some sort' signals rearranging the letters of FEEL BIAS; 'It's' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something feasible can be done, a straight synonym for possible.

clue.text: His leader expresses his opinion

parts.note: a newspaper's leader column is the leading article, written to carry the view of the man in charge of the paper

explanation.surface: A follower says that the boss speaks for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a chief, but in British newspapers a leader is the editorial column.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a newspaper sets its line, which the leading article states on his behalf.

clue.text: Side-track to avoid the start of trouble

parts.note: to shun something is to avoid it

indicators.note: the opening letter of trouble is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to take a detour so as to sidestep trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To shunt a train or a person is to move them onto a side track.

clue.text: Crack up, strangely enough

parts.note: to crack up is to collapse emotionally; oddly the phrase meaning the same thing points the other way, down instead of up

explanation.surface: Someone laughs or collapses, and it is somehow surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'strangely enough' is the joke: a phrase with 'down' means the same as one with 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervous collapse is said to crack someone up, the same as making them fall apart.

clue.text: Land on a site needing development

indicators.note: a site that needs development will be reworked, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A plot of land sits on a building site awaiting the developers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing development' rearranges ON A SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a country, and a country is a land.

clue.text: Some card games that may be supplied by a stationer

definitions.meaning: in bridge and whist a set of games won by the best of three is called by this name

definitions.text: that may be supplied by a stationer
definitions.meaning: a stationer sells erasers, which in British English share this name

explanation.surface: Card players are told their game can be bought at the stationer's.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a pencil eraser goes by the same name as a bridge match.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bridge match of three games and a pencil eraser.

clue.text: Wine jar I recycled when empty

indicators.note: jar and I are recycled, made over into a new arrangement

parts.note: empty means nothing, the letter O standing for zero

explanation.surface: A wine jar is sent to the recycling once drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' rearranges JAR I together with O, the zero that 'empty' gives; 'when' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Spanish region of the same name.

clue.text: Officer getting a rough ride on ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the second piece below the first, so the ship comes first

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

indicators.note: a rough ride is roughed up, the letters shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An officer has a choppy voyage aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges A RIDE to ADIER; in a down clue 'on' puts it below the ship. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer commanding a brigade.

clue.text: Time in its entirety?

indicators.note: with the question mark, 'in its' hints that the following word holds the letters in another form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about the whole span of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: endless time. The question mark marks the loose signal 'in its', which points to rearranging ENTIRETY.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, all of time taken together.

clue.text: Brood about one's ill-treatment

indicators.note: about means the musing word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to brood is to muse, think long and gloomily
one is I, and the 's is read as is, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone dwells gloomily on how badly they have been treated.
explanation.walkthrough: "One's" is read as 'one is', and 'about' wraps the brooding word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuse means abuse or wrong handling, a synonym of ill-treatment.

clue.text: Double-crosser, jailed more than once?

definitions.meaning: someone unfaithful to a partner, cheating on them in secret
read literally, someone who has done time twice, i.e. served two prison sentences

explanation.surface: A traitor turns out to be a repeat offender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing time' is prison slang; the question mark flags reading the word literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-timer cheats on a partner, a kind of double-crosser.

clue.text: Hide from the kids

parts.note: kids are young goats, and a hide is the skin of an animal

explanation.surface: Someone conceals something away from the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb about concealing; it is a noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather from goats, an animal hide taken from kids.

clue.text: Go away to see a relative about five

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go round the other one

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave and visit an aunt at five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts V inside A AUNT; 'to see' is a link. The answer is an archaic command to be gone.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned exclamation telling someone to leave, used as a dismissal like begone.

clue.text: Supporters groan — it stops play

indicators.note: play suggests the letters playing about, moving into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Fans groan when something brings the game to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like the game being stopped; it rearranges GROAN IT STOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Protagonists can mean advocates or champions of a cause, its supporters.

clue.text: He stops at break promptly!

indicators.note: break means smashing the words up so their letters can be reassembled

explanation.surface: A man stops promptly when the break comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' looks like an insertion signal, but HE STOPS AT is the fodder and 'break' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with great speed, as promptly as possible.

clue.text: Command one to go into the artillery

indicators.note: to go into says the next piece is placed inside

parts.note: ordnance means artillery and military supplies
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An order sends a soldier into the gunners.
explanation.walkthrough: Don't confuse the two spellings: ORDNANCE is guns, the answer a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative order or decree, a command.

clue.text: Develops way through mountain peaks

indicators.note: through means the way runs inside the peaks

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis
a road is a way

explanation.surface: A road is driven through the summits as a region develops.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is a Scottish word for a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden is to widen or expand, which is to develop.

clue.text: Key man in the penal system

definitions.text: Key man in the penal system

parts.words: Key man in the penal system
parts.note: looks like an important official; literally the man in prison who holds the keys

explanation.surface: A tribute to an important figure in criminal justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as important; here it is literal, the keys to the cells.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail guard carries the keys and works inside the prison system.

clue.text: Select a quiet spot

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
a point is a spot or place

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a peaceful place.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint is to choose someone for a post, to select.

clue.text: A kiss, say, indicates an attachment

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be spoken, giving the sound we want

parts.note: a kiss is X, so 'a kiss' is an X

explanation.surface: A kiss is a sign of affection or attachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an X', with X the kiss, spoken out is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building attached to a main one, an extension.

clue.text: Emotion shown by love in little ways

indicators.note: in means the love piece goes inside the paths

parts.note: paths are small ways or tracks
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Feeling is expressed through love's small gestures.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as O comes from tennis scoring; 'shown by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that arouses pity or sadness, a stirred emotion.

clue.text: Church council in controversy, no doubt

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gathering of clergy is no doubt mired in controversy.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church leaders, a church council.

clue.text: Fondness for a swan-song

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a chant is a song

explanation.surface: Someone has a liking for a swan song, a final performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swan-song' looks like one phrase; split it into its two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

clue.text: Unexpectedly met with greeting — not returned

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: returned says the word not is turned back to front

explanation.surface: An unexpected encounter, a greeting that went unanswered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on something is to come upon or discover it by chance.

clue.text: He has one pound, about to invest in foreign capital

indicators.note: about means the pound and one wrap round the other piece

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
I is the Roman numeral one
to sink money is to invest it

explanation.surface: A man with a pound to his name is about to invest it abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the surface's money talk: 'pound' is just L. 'has' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland, a capital abroad from Britain.

clue.text: Head girl is mace-bearer

parts.note: nut is slang for head
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A head girl carries the ceremonial mace.
explanation.walkthrough: Mace is also a spice made from the husk round the seed, so the definition is a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The nutmeg seed is wrapped in mace, the spice, so it bears mace.

clue.text: Going from Ringway to finish in Belgian port

parts.note: ring is O and way is ST, the abbreviation for street
end means finish

explanation.surface: A journey from Ringway airport ending in a Belgian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Ringway is the old name for Manchester Airport; here it splits as ring plus way. 'Going from' and 'to' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a seaport on the Belgian coast.

clue.text: Hastened out to see mountains

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hurried out to look at the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HASTENED; 'to see' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the mountain range running down western South America.
